sections.title: Description
sections.text: The Property, 47 St Giles Street is a principally two storey period Grade II Listed building with mezzanine, attic and extensive basement accommodation, forming part of the established historic townscape. The decorative Bath stone façade is executed in the neoclassical style with rusticated Tuscan columns and sash windows, giving the building strong architectural presence. Originally a 17th century house, the property was acquired by the Freemasons in 1879 and established as a Masonic Hall by 1881. The current structure was designed by Albert Havers and built in 1905–1906, with further remodelling in 1928. Until recently it operated as a Masonic club and events venue.

The property comprises a high yielding retail/funeralcare investment occupying a prominent pitch.
Arranged as a ground floor retail unit with associated upper parts and a yard to the rear, the property is fully let to Funeral Services Limited t/a Coop Funeralcare on a newly signed 10 year lease expiring 10.12.2034 and paying £18,000 per annum.
The tenant is a long standing occupier, and whilst the lease was signed in September 2026 the lease commencement was back-dated to December 2024 which was the expiry of the previous lease. We consider this displays continued commitment to the location.
We are unaware of the current use of the upper parts, but understand it may be used as residential accommodation. We consider the property may benefit from potential to convert these upper parts to residential uses if not (subject to the existing lease and any requisite consents).
The property occupies a prominent pitch fronting Newbold Road at the junction with Highfield Lane and forms part of a local retail parade. The surrounding area is characterised by residential uses.

sections.title: Further Information
sections.text: Mexborough town centre is undergoing a major, multi-year regeneration programme, with approximately £24 million in funding secured for upgrades, according to 2026 reports from the City of Doncaster Council. The project, which is already underway, aims to revitalize the High Street, improve transport links, and boost the local economy. Building owners and tenants of retail properties on High Street and York Square in Mexborough town centre will be able to apply for a grant of up to £10,000 towards visual improvements to shop frontages. The grant does not need to be repaid and it can be spent on a wide range of improvements.

sections.title: Description
sections.text:
The buyer will be required to enter into an Deed of Overage in the approximate form set out in the legal pack provided. In summary, the Deed of Overage provides that an overage of 33.33% of any uplift in respect of each and every planning permission or general change of use from the Permitted Use (being agricultural or equestrian use) during the Overage Period shall be payable to the seller on the earlier of (i) implementation of a relevant planning or (ii) the sale of the property with the benefit of a relevant planning permission. The Overage Period will run for a period of 30 years from and including the date of completion. The above is intended as a summary of the terms only . You are encouraged to review the Deed of Overage in full, and to take legal advice on the terms of the same.
Part of the land is impacted by the Hynet CO2 pipeline being constructed to carry CO2 from Liverpool to the sea bed. This is largely limited to a strip no wider than 24.4m across the land.
The Development Consent Order was in force 16th October 2024 and works have started on site.
Whilst Heads of Terms have been drafted these have not been documented.
A report on the position and options for compensation and or lease of the sub surface has been commissioned by the Vendor from Carter Jonas which is available in the legal pack - "Hawardan Estate Reduced Report"
It is intended that the negotiations and any settlements are transferred to the buyer from completion.
The tenants are separately pursuing their own negotiations.

sections.text:
The property comprises part ground and extensive upper floor accommodation within the historic Royal Arcade, extending to approximately 2,189 sq m (23,562 sq ft) and benefitting from Planning Permission and Listed Building Consent for conversion and refurbishment to provide a 33-unit residential scheme together with six office suites.
A residential scheme has been drawn up which illustrates the potential to create a substantial number of residential units above and/or behind the commercial accommodation, subject to the necessary consents.
The property comprises the extensive upper floors of the historic Royal Arcade in the heart of Bournemouth town centre, presenting a rare opportunity to deliver a substantial residential-led refurbishment and conversion project with the planning position already established.
The accommodation extends to approximately 2,183 sq m (23,500 sq ft) and benefits from Planning Permission and Listed Building Consent for the creation of a 33-unit residential scheme comprising a mix of one, two and three-bedroom apartments. Significantly, a substantial proportion of the accommodation already benefited from established residential use and consent, with further planning permissions subsequently secured for the additional units required to complete the approved scheme.
The majority of the proposed apartments are already physically formed within the existing building configuration, having been historically occupied as residential accommodation. Numerous units retain substantial masonry divisions and existing layouts, with drainage infrastructure remaining at former residential locations, albeit purchasers should rely on their own investigations regarding condition and suitability.
The approved scheme provides an attractive mix of accommodation, including numerous duplex apartments together with a number of generously proportioned two and three-bedroom units, several extending to in excess of 100 sq m. In addition, the property includes six office suites extending to approximately 306 sq m (3,294 sq ft), offering future asset management and potential development opportunities, subject to obtaining any necessary consents.
Extensive sound testing has already been undertaken and a priced schedule of works has been prepared, providing purchasers with a significant body of due diligence information.
Estimated Rental Values
- Residential and office rental appraisal indicating an aggregate estimated rental value of approximately £495,660 per annum. Interested parties should rely on their own enquiries.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: The site extends to approximately 17.6acres (7.12 ha) and is located to the rear of the ASDA store and Larkhall Academy’s sports pitches. Consisting of a mixture of scrub vegetation and open ground set within existing mature woodland, the site provides an established environment to develop within.  Lovell Homes have now completed the development of 97 units on the land to the south which have all been sold.  Access to the site is either via Montgomerie Avenue or Broomhill Drive at the northern side of the site (and adjacent to Asda). A hammerhead currently exists where an access road into the site can be made.  The site benefits from excellent views west towards the Larkhall viaduct, Cherry Hill and Millheugh Bridge.  The old railway line which links to the viaduct over the Avon Water provides a picturesque walking route. The adjoining land to the west of the site is protected as a Site of Special Scientific Interest which again adds to the attraction of the landscape.

The property comprises a detached steel portal frame industrial unit providing a combination of warehouse, office, training and ancillary accommodation. The building is clad with insulated profile sheet elevations beneath a combination of multi-pitched, mono-pitched and flat roof sections.
The warehouse benefits from two roller shutter loading doors, LED lighting, WC facilities and a suspended ceiling, with an internal height of approximately 6.1 metres.
Ancillary accommodation is arranged over ground and first floors and includes offices, storage areas, staff welfare facilities and training rooms.
The first-floor office accommodation is fitted to a higher specification, incorporating LED lighting, perimeter trunking and electric space heating.
Externally, the property benefits from a substantial secure concrete yard extending across the frontage and wrapping around the building, providing vehicle access from both Cumberland Street and Bromley Street and facilitating loading, circulation and operational requirements.

sections.text: The property is situated in the affluent South West London district of Fulham, prominently located on the north side of King’s Road (A308), a renowned retailing and leisure thoroughfare, in close proximity to Chelsea. The property is situated some 300 metres from Stamford Bridge stadium and 400 metres from Fulham Broadway Underground Station (District Line - Zone 2). King's Road Park, a significant residential development, is located approximately 60 metres from the property and will provide 1,800-1,850 new homes across five phases, bringing a significant increase in local residential population and driving footfall for future leisure uses. Nearby occupiers include a wide range of high-end retailers, independent boutiques, restaurants, cafés and leisure operators, with the immediate section of King’s Road providing a vibrant and well-established local retail and leisure offering. Notable occupiers nearby include Warr’s Harley-Davidson, Design Centre Chelsea Harbour, Tesco Express and a range of prominent furniture, interior design and lifestyle brands.

sections.text: Monmouth is an historic market town situated in south-east Wales, close to the borders of Herefordshire and Gloucestershire. Renowned for its historic character and architectural heritage, Monmouth is a popular tourist destination, benefiting from its setting within the Wye Valley and proximity to Brecon Beacons National Park. Agincourt House is situated on Agincourt Square, in the heart of Monmouth town centre. The property occupies a prominent position within the historic square, close to Monnow Street, the town's principal retailing thoroughfare. Nearby occupiers include M&S Foodhall, Pizza Express, Caffe Nero, Costa Coffee, Superdrug, Boots and Mountain Warehouse.

sections.text: The site extends to approximately 17.6acres (7.12 ha) and is located to the rear of the ASDA store and Larkhall Academy’s sports pitches. Consisting of a mixture of scrub vegetation and open ground set within existing mature woodland, the site provides an established environment to develop within.  Lovell Homes have now completed the development of 97 units on the land to the south which have all been sold.  Access to the site is either via Montgomerie Avenue or Broomhill Drive at the northern side of the site (and adjacent to Asda). sections.text: The lot comprises a vacant former concert hall dating from 1914, recognised as a non-designated heritage asset, on a large site of approximately 3,057 sq m (32,907 sq ft). Drawings of the proposed plans are available for inspection upon request.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A long leasehold interest comprising the flank wall of a mixed-use building arranged over ground and two upper storeys. The wall accommodates an established commercial advertising structure operating since 2002 as a 48-sheet digital advertising display (having historically operated as an Ultra Vision rotating display and a scroller unit prior to digital conversion in 2018).

sections.title: Tenure
sections.text: Important registration information: The leasehold title being sold is not currently registered at HM Land Registry. An application to register the lease was submitted but has since been cancelled by HM Land Registry following correspondence regarding outstanding registration issues. The position remains unresolved, and any further application will be subject to satisfying HM Land Registry's requirements. The successful buyer will acquire the unregistered leasehold interest and will need to take account of the outstanding registration issues and any further steps required to secure registration.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Situated on the south side of Lillie Road near its junction with Pellant Road, adjacent to Sir John Lillie Nursery and Primary School within the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham. Lillie Road forms part of the A3218, running west from West Brompton (District Line and London Overground services) towards Fulham Palace Road (A219), intersecting with North End Road and Munster Road. The immediate vicinity comprises a mixed-use commercial and residential locality benefitting from substantial pedestrian and vehicular traffic.

sections.title: Description
sections.text:
The property comprises a freehold light industrial investment extending to approximately 2,661 sq ft (247.30 sq m), currently occupied by a gym operator on a licence agreement producing £6,000 per annum.
We consider the property offers clear asset management potential, with the opportunity to regear the existing occupation and secure a longer-term lease arrangement.The property may also be suitable for alternative uses, subject to obtaining the requisite consents.
The property is situated within an established light industrial parade accessed from both Dear Street and Market Place, the principal retail pitch in Market Rasen. The surrounding area is characterised by a mix of similar light industrial and commercial occupiers.
